name: Highlands 18

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, with a paved driveway curving from the road toward a circular turnaround in front of the main residence|The residence is a multi-section, single-story structure with flat and low-pitched rooflines and earth-toned masonry exterior walls|A detached structure with a light metal roof is visible to the right of the main residence, connected by the paved driveway loop|Scattered juniper and pine trees surround the property on all sides, with a manicured lawn area visible behind the main structure|The street frontage opens directly onto the paved road to the right of the scene.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property from the road-adjacent perspective, where the paved driveway entrance connects to the curved road|The detached structure with a metal roof is clearly visible on this side, positioned northeast of the main residence|Dense tree coverage on the right flank limits direct lateral access to the property from this side|The driveway curves inward from the road, providing the primary vehicle access route visible from this angle.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, which is heavily screened by dense juniper and pine trees extending well beyond the lawn area|The rear yard transitions from maintained lawn to natural desert terrain with no visible secondary access routes from the rear|The main residence roof sections are partially visible through the tree canopy|No rear gates, outbuildings, or pathways leading away from the structure are visible from this perspective.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, where the multi-section residence extends across the parcel with its low-pitched rooflines visible among the surrounding trees|A grassed area is visible to the rear-left of the structure, flanked by dense tree cover on the left perimeter|No fencing, gates, or secondary driveways are visible along the left side|Access from the left side of the property is limited to foot travel through open desert terrain between trees.

considerations: The property is accessed by a single curved paved driveway connecting to the adjacent road, terminating at a circular turnaround in front of the main residence, which provides adequate apparatus staging. Dense juniper and pine trees surround the property on all sides except the front driveway approach, significantly limiting lateral and rear responder access and sightlines. The rear and left side of the property are accessible only on foot through natural desert terrain. The detached structure with a metal roof northeast of the main residence requires responders to navigate the driveway loop to reach it.
clarifications: Does the circular turnaround in front of the residence provide sufficient clearance for large emergency apparatus? Is there any gate or access control at the driveway entrance from the road? What is the surface condition of the driveway, and can it support heavy vehicle loads? Does the detached structure have its own entry door and use, such as a garage or separate living space? Are there any locked gates or barriers between the main residence and the rear lawn area?
